thread:
alice: Quick heads-up — noticed a bunch of support tickets where customers are confused by the console "dialplan" for v1/v2 routing. My rough take: the current console shows a single "version preference" toggle per route but doesn't surface quota or sampling implications.
ben: +1, saw similar in logs — customers flip the toggle and expect immediate cutover, but our backend does a sampled canary then affinity. Not obvious.
carla: Are there concrete examples? screenshots?
alice: Yep — ticket 4532: customer toggled prefer-v2, then got a 10% v1 traffic for 48h because of session affinity. They thought it was a bug.
dave: Oof. That suggests our UI/UX copy and telemetry aren't aligned. We show "Prefer v2" but telemetry & routing do "gradual co-existence".
emily: We intentionally do that for safety (rollouts + regression protection). But we can clarify in console and add an expandable "How this works" panel.
ben: Also quotas — if a tenant is near v2 quota, we automatically route to v1 as fallback. Console currently doesn't show quota headroom in the toggle. Customers get surprised when their traffic hits fallback.
carla: Proposal: change toggle to a multi-state control: Off / Prefer v2 (gradual) / Force v2 (hard). Force v2 should be gated behind an API flag + SRE approval.
dave: I like that. UX note: show expected % over time (e.g., 0 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100) for Prefer mode and show real-time sampling signal.
emily: From infra side, we need to expose two telemetry signals to the console: 1) route-sample-rate (what % is being sampled to v2), 2) fallback-reason (quota|latency|error|manual). Those are already in traces but not aggregated per-route.
ben: Can we add a small per-route micro-dashboard that shows those two metrics and a toggle state timeline? Minimal — just sparkline + current value.
alice: Agree. Also need to update API to accept explicit rollout_mode: "off"|"prefer_gradual"|"force" and add rollout_metadata {target_pct, reason}. Then console maps its UI to that API.
carla: Important: existing clients hitting v1/v2 headers should keep working. We must ensure backward-compat of the route control API. Add a compatibility param `legacy_opt_in` that maps old toggles to new semantics.
dave: Telemetry: add events when a route transitions states (user toggles), plus any automated fallback kicks. These should be tagged with tenant_id, route_id, and reason.
emily: Implementation plan: infra: expose sample-rate and fallback-reason in the routing decision log aggregator (1 week). API: new rollout_mode + rollout_metadata (2 days). Console: new control states + micro-dashboard (3 days design + 4 days dev).
ben: Can we short-circuit Force v2 in console behind a ribbon: "Call SRE to approve force changes" rather than programmatic block? Less friction for small teams.
carla: For enterprise customers we should require an audit log and an approval workflow (legal/compliance ask). So make Force v2 require an audit flag in the API and record the approver in the event.
alice: Also add a tooltip: "Prefer v2: we will progressively shift ephemeral sessions; session affinity may keep some users on v1 for up to 72h." copy reviewed by product.
dave: Edge case: what happens to long-lived streaming sessions when we change preference? We must ensure we never split an active connection mid-stream. That's already true in runtime but add an explicit note.
emily: Runtime: yes, we don't reassign existing connections. We'll log any reassign attempts as warnings.
ben: Testing: add a smoke e2e that flips route to Prefer and checks sampled distribution matches expected +/-5% after 1k requests. Add a canary test for Force mode too.
alice: Next steps: emily to open infra task to surface the two signals; ben to draft API spec for rollout_mode + legacy_opt_in; carla to prototype console mockups; dave to update runbook for Force mode approvals.
emily: I'll start the infra ticket today: infra/route-telemetry #784.
ben: I'll drop an API spec PR: api/rollouts#12.
carla: Mockups incoming by EOD Thursday.
dave: I'll add Force-mode approval section to the runbook and flag SRE for a sync.
deploy-bot: Note: deploy job for routing-telemetry-service passed on staging (build 2026-03-21_14:05).
alice: Thanks all — aim to pair on the console wording once mockups are ready. Small ask: add a quick changelog entry to the console release notes about the 3-state toggle and telemetry dashboard.
emily: Will do.
carla: One last thing — add a short opt-out header for SDK teams: `X-Redwood-Route-Mode: legacy` so SDKs can explicitly opt legacy semantics if they can't handle gradual changes.
dave: Good call. Include that in the API spec.
alice: OK wrapping up. I'll summarize in the design doc and link tickets. Thanks!
